content.text: Digital creators in Venezuela face a critical challenge: accepting crypto payments. The inability to use Stripe or PayPal leaves them without a reliable payment gateway. When traditional payment solutions fail, creators are left to navigate a complex web of workarounds and compromises. In this article, we'll explore the infrastructure that solves this problem at its core and provide a concrete plan for implementation.
The Real Reason This Problem Exists

This problem exists because of the reliance on third-party payment processors. When countries impose restrictions on these processors, creators are left without a solution. The issue is not just about Venezuela; it's about the lack of sovereignty in commerce infrastructure. Creators need a solution that allows them to control their finances, manage their payments, and avoid dependence on external services. This requires a fundamental shift in how commerce infrastructure is designed and implemented.
Why the Obvious Fixes Do Not Work

Obvious fixes, such as using alternative payment processors or workarounds, only provide temporary relief. These solutions often come with significant fees, complex setup processes, and limited scalability. They do not address the underlying issue of sovereignty in commerce infrastructure. Creators need a solution that is robust, scalable, and independent of external services. This requires a base-layer infrastructure that allows creators to manage their finances independently.
The Infrastructure That Solves It at the Base Layer

Cloudflare Pages and GitHub Pages both provide free static site hosting that works identically regardless of where the server operator is located. A store deployed on Cloudflare Pages by a creator in Harare is served from Cloudflare's global edge network — the same infrastructure that serves enterprises in New York. GitHub Pages is backed by Microsoft's global infrastructure. Neither platform imposes geographic restrictions on who can deploy a store or who can access it. Combined with NOWPayments for payment processing and Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, this creates a complete commerce infrastructure with zero hosting costs and no geographic restrictions at any layer of the stack.
The key to a sovereign commerce infrastructure is independence from external services.
